newsitem.title: DUBAI: Amoco announces Nile Delta gas discovery.
newsitem.headline: Amoco announces Nile Delta gas discovery.

text.p: U.S. oil firm Amoco Corp said on Thursday it had made a significant gas discovery at its offshore North Sinai concession in Egypt's Nile Delta.
Tao-1 discovery well drilled 35 miles (56 km) offshore tested at 37.9 million cubic feet of gas a day.

"The test results from this well indicate outstanding deliverability from the zone tested which is similar in quality to the other zones encountered," Denis Mascardelli, Amoco Egypt's vice president for exploration said in a statement.
Amoco Egypt president and general manager Bob Sheppard said that the new discovery was further convincing evidence of the importance of the Nile Delta as a major gas basin.

"The eastern Mediterranean is a major strategic area for Amoco...our continuing exploration success bodes well for our plans, together with the Egyptian government, to develop this area as a major regional natural gas hub," Sheppard said.
Amoco signed a memorandum of understanding with Egyptian and Turkish entities in 1996 for the development of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports from the Nile Delta to Turkey.
"Amoco with its partners is also examining the feasibility of supplying gas to near regional markets," the statement.
Jordanian Energy Minister Hashem Dabbas said on Wednesday that Amoco had signed a deal to study building a pipeline to export Egyptain gas to Jordan.
